note: Both sets cover the same core Cooking thresholds and dinner-party facts and both repeat the same facts once per unit, but A additionally misbinds five reduced-point mass values to "kitchen appliance" instead of the Cooking Subcontest and adds two graph "points trend" claims whose quotes are only axis labels and do not support them. B keeps every value bound to the Cooking Subcontest or the stated entity and adds the village/neighborhood count of 5, which A omits. Neither set is free of duplication, and both leave out notable facts such as the two dinner parties per team, the eight-person guest list limit, the 11 p.m. submission deadline, and the 0%–100% score range.
remarks: Both extractions restate each threshold once per unit (lb/oz/kg/g), inflating claim counts with duplicates. A's two "points trend" claims are visible in Figure 9 but their quotes are merely the axis titles, so they are unsupported as quoted. Important facts both sets miss: two dinner parties per team during contest week, guest list limited to eight people, scores submitted by 11 p.m., percentage integer scores ranging 0%–100%, and the requirement that the kitchen appliance operate in its normal configuration.
